section_summary: This section traces Allied negotiations over the Japanese fleet after the surrender: which warships to destroy, when to divide smaller combat vessels, and how to use Japanese shipping for repatriation. It also contains French claims for ships and naval matériel in Indochina, a veterans’ proposal to exhibit a captured submarine, and committee papers opposing an immediate transfer of vessels to the Soviet Union.

people.name: John Carter Vincent
people.role: State Department Far Eastern Affairs official

people.name: H. Freeman Matthews
people.role: State Department official; acting SWNCC chairman

people.name: J. K. Penfield
people.role: Office of Far Eastern Affairs official

people.name: R. L. Dennison
people.role: U.S. Navy captain and Assistant Chief of Naval Operations for Politico-Military Affairs

people.name: H. H. Croy
people.role: U.S. Naval Reserve lieutenant and submarine veteran

people.name: Donald C. Blaisdell
people.role: Acting Chief, Division of International Security Affairs

people.name: A. J. McFarland
people.role: Brigadier General, U.S. Army; Joint Chiefs of Staff secretary

subfiles.title: Ship-sinking consultation
subfiles.about: Vincent explains confusion over whether to consult other governments before sinking surrendered Japanese ships.
subfiles.summary: Vincent reports that Dunn and Hickerson will review the issue and that Nimitz has been told to withhold action.

subfiles.title: Telegram 2175 to Moscow
subfiles.to: U.S. ambassador in Moscow, for Vyacheslav Molotov
subfiles.about: Byrnes invites Molotov’s views on sinking surrendered Japanese fleet units.
subfiles.summary: Byrnes recalls his London discussion and asks for an early Soviet response before advising the Navy.

subfiles.title: Top Secret cover sheet for telegram 2175
subfiles.about: Control form records routing of the October 17, 1945 Moscow telegram.
subfiles.summary: Cover sheet and reverse-side handling instructions.

subfiles.title: Telegram 3594 from Moscow
subfiles.about: Harriman reports Molotov’s initial response to the proposal to sink the Japanese fleet.
subfiles.summary: Molotov requests time to consult naval authorities and asks whether all surface ships and submarines are included. He also seeks updated figures on the fleet; Harriman has none beyond an August estimate.

subfiles.title: Top Secret cover sheet for telegram 3594
subfiles.about: Control form identifies Harriman’s October 18 telegram.
subfiles.summary: Cover sheet and reverse-side handling instructions.

subfiles.title: Telegram 2197 to Moscow
subfiles.to: W. Averell Harriman, for Vyacheslav Molotov
subfiles.about: Byrnes accepts Molotov’s proposed fleet disposition and discusses the merchant marine.
subfiles.summary: Byrnes agrees to the fleet plan, says merchant ships remain needed for repatriation, and offers later Allied talks on their distribution.

subfiles.title: Top Secret cover sheet for telegram 2197
subfiles.about: Control form identifies the October 20 telegram to Moscow.
subfiles.summary: Cover sheet and reverse-side handling instructions.

subfiles.title: Handwritten note on briefing Harriman
subfiles.about: A brief note recommends giving Harriman the information he requested.
subfiles.summary: Recommends supplying Harriman with background.

subfiles.title: Disposition of Japanese Merchant Marine
subfiles.about: Gardiner reports that merchant-marine disposal policy is still being drafted.
subfiles.summary: A Shipping Division draft is expected by the SWNCC Far Eastern Subcommittee on November 1.

subfiles.title: Advice on reply to Molotov about merchant shipping
subfiles.about: Matthews suggests a response to Molotov on Japanese merchant ships.
subfiles.summary: He says repatriation needs currently take priority and recommends offering future Allied talks on final disposition.

subfiles.title: Telegram 3617 from Moscow
subfiles.about: Harriman requests the text of Molotov’s October 19 fleet proposal.
subfiles.summary: He seeks background on the proposal Byrnes accepted and reports delivering telegram 2197.

subfiles.title: Top Secret cover sheet for telegram 3617
subfiles.about: Control form identifies Harriman’s October 21 telegram.
subfiles.summary: Cover sheet and reverse-side handling instructions.

subfiles.title: Telegram 2199 to Moscow
subfiles.about: The Department supplies Molotov’s October 19 proposal.
subfiles.summary: Molotov accepts scuttling large warships and submarines, claims one quarter of smaller vessels, and asks about merchant ships.

subfiles.title: Top Secret cover sheet for telegram 2199
subfiles.about: Control form identifies the October 22 telegram to Moscow.
subfiles.summary: Cover sheet and reverse-side handling instructions.

subfiles.title: Additional copy of telegram 3617
subfiles.about: This is another filed copy of Harriman’s request for Molotov’s proposal.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the request and confirms delivery of Byrnes’s message.

subfiles.title: Request for statement on Japanese fleet
subfiles.about: Brown asks Matthews to coordinate a public statement on fleet disposition.
subfiles.summary: Requests continued contact about a statement for the Secretary.

subfiles.title: Questions on informing Britain and China
subfiles.about: Vincent seeks instructions before approaching British and Chinese representatives.
subfiles.summary: He asks whether Army and Navy should be informed and whether Britain and China are being consulted or merely notified.

subfiles.title: Further question on Allied notification
subfiles.about: A note relays Vincent’s concern about how to describe the fleet decision.
subfiles.summary: Vincent prefers presenting it as a U.S. decision without invoking agreement with the Soviets.

subfiles.title: Notification of Chinese and British representatives
subfiles.about: Vincent reports telling Wei Tao Ming and George Sansom of the U.S. fleet decision.
subfiles.summary: He described destruction of large ships and equal four-power division of smaller vessels without mentioning Soviet talks; both said they would notify their governments.

subfiles.title: Charge-out card for Vincent memorandum
subfiles.about: A file card tracks removal of the October 26 Vincent memorandum.
subfiles.summary: Records file 894.30/10-2645 and later handling marks.

subfiles.title: British view on Japanese Navy disposition
subfiles.about: Dunn forwards a British Embassy note on the Japanese Navy.
subfiles.summary: He reports that Britain knows the U.S. position and expects later discussions between naval officials and the British Joint Staff Mission.

subfiles.title: Return of SWNCC file
subfiles.about: SWNCC returns the British-position file after Dunn’s memorandum was introduced.
subfiles.summary: Explains that the memorandum was addressed to SWNCC because the Army also had an interest.

subfiles.title: Charge-out card for December memorandum
subfiles.about: A file card tracks the December 12 Japanese-fleet memorandum.
subfiles.summary: Records file 894.30/12-1245 and handling marks.

subfiles.title: Other file charge-out card
subfiles.about: A largely illegible charge-out card records a separately filed item.
subfiles.summary: Subject and identifying details are obscured by OCR noise.

subfiles.title: French claim to Japanese naval vessels
subfiles.about: France requests a share of the Japanese fleet and use of Japanese naval matériel in Indochina.
subfiles.summary: The note cites French naval losses, damage to Saigon’s naval yard, and French service against Japan. It seeks a large surface vessel, preferably an aircraft carrier, four modern destroyers, replacement harbor equipment, and access to matériel in Indochina.

subfiles.title: Translation of French note of January 8
subfiles.about: English translation of France’s January 8 claim.
subfiles.summary: Repeats the account of French losses and wartime service, and the requests for ships, harbor equipment, and naval matériel.

subfiles.title: Comment on French naval matériel claim
subfiles.about: Martin assesses French rights to Japanese matériel captured in Indochina.
subfiles.summary: He treats military matériel as war booty under theater-command policy and other Japanese property as chargeable against French reparations claims.

subfiles.title: Request for Navy views on French claim
subfiles.about: Penfield asks the Navy for advice on replying to France.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the French note’s translation and Martin’s comments.

subfiles.title: Draft reply to French ambassador
subfiles.about: The United States responds to French requests for Japanese ships and matériel.
subfiles.summary: The draft leaves Indochinese naval matériel to military commanders and links other property to reparations policy. It supports destroying large combatants and is willing in principle to transfer some smaller vessels from the U.S. share once SCAP no longer needs them.

subfiles.title: French supplementary naval-loss note
subfiles.about: France supplies details supporting its claim to Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: The note describes the Richelieu’s operations and presents an itemized list of French ships lost in the Far East, with tonnage and circumstances. It reiterates the importance France places on receiving a share of the Japanese fleet.

subfiles.title: Translation of French supplementary note
subfiles.about: English translation of the January 22 French naval-loss note.
subfiles.summary: The translation repeats France’s account of the Richelieu’s service and its detailed vessel-loss list, including ships sunk or scuttled in Indochina.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of French correspondence to Paris
subfiles.to: Officer in Charge, American Mission, Paris
subfiles.about: State sends Paris copies of French fleet claims and the Department’s reply.
subfiles.summary: Transmits two French notes and the March 1 U.S. response for information.

subfiles.title: Navy response on French claims
subfiles.about: Dennison recommends a U.S. position on French requests for ships and matériel.
subfiles.summary: He supports possible transfer of smaller ships from the U.S. share, subject to policy, and theater-command control over matériel in Indochina.

subfiles.title: SWNCC 186/12 transmittal to Far Eastern Commission representative
subfiles.about: State forwards the approved SWNCC report on Soviet claims to Japanese vessels.
subfiles.summary: Encloses SWNCC 186/12 for confidential information.

subfiles.title: SWNCC approval of paper 186/12
subfiles.from: H. Freeman Matthews, acting chairman, SWNCC
subfiles.about: SWNCC approves its report on transfer of Japanese smaller combatants to the Soviet Union.
subfiles.summary: Requests implementation, transmission to the Far Eastern Commission representative, and a message to Moscow; bars press release.

subfiles.title: SWNCC 186/12 signature routing
subfiles.about: A routing slip sends the SWNCC memorandum for Matthews’s signature.
subfiles.summary: Marked for Matthews’s signature.

subfiles.title: File note for SWNCC letter and enclosures
subfiles.about: A file note identifies the committee letter and enclosures about Soviet transfer of destroyers.
subfiles.summary: Indexes the SWNCC package; its typed year appears erroneous.

subfiles.title: SWNCC 186/12: Transfer to Soviet Union of Japanese vessels
subfiles.from: State-War-Navy Coordinating Subcommittee for the Far East
subfiles.about: The report evaluates Soviet requests for immediate division of Japanese warships and merchant ships.
subfiles.summary: SWNCC recommends retaining SCAP control of vessels needed for repatriation and surrender tasks, postponing division of smaller combatants until those tasks end, and leaving merchant-fleet disposal to broader reparations and economic decisions. Its appendices recount Allied agreements and Soviet requests, discuss repatriation from Soviet-held areas, and draft a message to Moscow. Several pages contain duplicate copies of report text.

subfiles.title: Croy cover letter to Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Croy forwards a veterans’ petition about a captured Japanese submarine.
subfiles.summary: He asks for assistance if the proposal comes within State’s purview.

subfiles.title: Petition to exhibit a Japanese submarine
subfiles.from: H. H. Croy and fellow submarine veterans
subfiles.to: United Nations Organization, National Contingents of Armed Forces Committee
subfiles.about: Veterans ask to buy or lease a captured Japanese submarine for public exhibitions.
subfiles.summary: They propose touring ports with one of five submarines at Pearl Harbor, after removal of sensitive equipment, and charging visitors admission.

subfiles.title: Request to draft reply to Croy
subfiles.about: Blaisdell asks for an acknowledgment of Croy’s letter.
subfiles.summary: He requests a draft along the lines of Thompson’s notation.

subfiles.title: Reply to H. H. Croy
subfiles.about: State acknowledges the submarine exhibition proposal.
subfiles.summary: Blaisdell directs Croy to the Navy for information and advice on the vessels.

subfiles.title: SWNCC memorandum on shipping information from Soviet areas
subfiles.from: John H. Hilldring, SWNCC state member
subfiles.about: SWNCC asks State to supplement its message to Moscow about Japanese shipping.
subfiles.summary: The committee urges a request for Soviet data on captured vessels and repatriation needs so SCAP can allocate shipping fairly.

subfiles.title: SWNCC 186/13 and Joint Chiefs’ memorandum
subfiles.from: Joint Chiefs of Staff; A. J. McFarland, secretary
subfiles.about: The Joint Chiefs seek information before additional Japanese vessels are assigned to Soviet use.
subfiles.summary: They warn that the earlier note might invite unsupported shipping demands. They propose requiring figures for Japanese vessels already held by Soviet forces and clear repatriation requirements, enabling SCAP to coordinate and allocate available shipping. Pages 76 and 77 partly duplicate one another.

subfiles.title: Telegram 836 to Moscow
subfiles.about: State instructs its embassy to supplement the Soviet shipping message.
subfiles.summary: The telegram asks Moscow to provide data on Japanese shipping in Soviet hands and the purposes for which it seeks more vessels, allowing SCAP to make equitable assignments.
